set_title: Sharp chest pain after a virus: pericardium, myocardium, pleura or chest wall
stem: A 16-year-old boy has had 3 days of sharp left chest pain that lasts seconds and is worse when he twists. He is afebrile. Pressing over the left fourth costochondral junction reproduces the pain. Heart, lungs and ECG are normal.
oneliner: 16M + sharp left chest pain lasting seconds + worse with twisting + reproduced by pressing a costochondral junction + normal heart, lungs, ECG → ?
ask: Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

whyNot.B: Pericarditis gives a **rub and diffuse ST elevation**; his ECG and heart exam are normal
whyNot.C: Myocarditis causes **dyspnea or a gallop**; his heart exam is normal
whyNot.D: Pleurodynia follows an enteroviral illness with **fever and paroxysms**; he is afebrile and his pain lasts seconds
whyNot.E: MI at 16 with **normal ECG and pain lasting seconds** reproduced by palpation is not infarction

why: Pain that is **reproduced by pressing the costochondral junction** with a normal heart, lungs and ECG is chest-wall inflammation. Tietze syndrome is the swollen, tender variant.

head: Pain character and position
ECG
Exam clue
Heart function
rows: Pericarditis
Sharp, pleuritic pain; worse supine, better sitting forward
Diffuse concave ST elevation with PR depression
**Pericardial friction rub (scratching, up to three components)**
Normal; an effusion may be present
Myocardial infarction
Pressure or crushing pain radiating to the arm or jaw; not positional
**Regional ST elevation with reciprocal depression; later Q waves**
Sweating, S4; murmur depends on the territory
Regional wall-motion abnormality
Viral myocarditis
Mild or absent chest pain; dyspnea dominates, after a viral illness
Sinus tachycardia, nonspecific ST-T changes
S3 gallop, signs of heart failure
**Dilated ventricle with reduced ejection fraction**; troponin raised
Pleurodynia
Paroxysmal stabbing chest-wall muscle pain, worse with breathing or movement; coxsackie B outbreaks in summer
**Normal**
Fever; no rub; tender intercostal muscles
Normal
Costochondritis
Brief, sharp pain, worse with movement or deep breaths
Normal
**Pain reproduced by pressing the costochondral junction**; heart and lungs normal
Normal
Pneumonia
Pleuritic pain on the side of the infection
Normal or sinus tachycardia
**Fever, productive cough, focal crackles or dullness**; consolidation on x-ray
Normal

idea.rule: Chest pain you can reproduce by palpation, normal ECG = costochondritis.
also: Pain worsens with deep breaths and movement
Diagnosis of exclusion after the dangerous causes are considered
